newsitem.title: PERU: INTERVIEW - Citibank sees payoff in Peru in two yrs.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Citibank sees payoff in Peru in two yrs.

text.p: Citibank in Peru said it was not especially concerned about showing a net loss in the first half because it expected investments to attract individual customers and expand its share in pension funds to reap solid results within two years.

In the first half of the year, Citibank was one of only three companies in Peru's growing banking sector to record a loss -- $476,000, compared with net profit of $1.3 million in the same period last year.

"The profit is not a theme that particularly worries us because the results will be seen in the next two years," the bank's director general in Peru, Gustavo Marin, said in an interview, referring to the results of its investment program. He did not give details of the plan.
Citibank, a unit of Citicorp, based in the United States, is the 17th largest of the 25 private banks operating in Peru. The operation is small by its international standards.
The company, which has a strong portfolio of corporate clients, is aiming to grow in Peru by focusing on building its base of individual customers to the bank, Marin said.
Citibank also saw room for growth by investing more in Peru's private pension funds, which industry officials estimate will double in size by 2,000.
It plans to buy more shares in one of Peru's five private pension funds, Profuturo, where it currently has a 22 percent stake, Marin said.
"The pension funds are very important because they are going to become the principal institutional investors in the country," he said.
Citibank believes the government's success in lowering inflation and generating steady growth has bolstered investor confidence in Peru.

That could attract banks from Argentina and Brazil to enter the local market, swelling the number of foreign-owned concerns already operating in Lima, including banks from the United States, Spain, Chile and Ecuador, Marin said.
